articles.title: Why sex differences in throwing cannot be explained by socialization alone
articles.summary: Is the pronounced gap in throwing ability between men and women purely a product of childhood socialization? A new commentary argues that evolutionary biology and social experience actually work hand-in-hand to shape this distinct sex difference.

articles.title: How online toxicity silences the majority and fuels power users
articles.summary: A recent field experiment on Reddit reveals why a vocal minority dominates online political discussions, finding that toxic environments silence the majority while fueling the most active users.

The two entries above it belong to the leaderboard's agentic category, multi-step systems that use agents or language models to reason about, generate or select forecasts. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy interventions propagate through public communication, institutional decisions, and stakeholder responses, yet datasets for financial multi-agent simulation rarely connect these processes to temporally aligned historical evidence. articles.title: Scientists identify the nose-to-brain circuit that makes slow breathing calming
articles.summary: New research shows that slow nasal breathing directly reduces anxiety by activating a specific nose-to-brain circuit, while fast breathing worsens it. The findings, published in PNAS, suggest the physical rhythm of airflow acts as an emotional dial.

articles.title: Midlife belly fat is linked to elevated Alzheimer’s biomarkers decades later
articles.summary: Tracking body fat over a 35-year period reveals that excess belly fat in midlife is linked to a higher risk of Alzheimer’s disease decades later. However, the relationship reverses in old age as cognitive decline alters metabolism.

articles.title: Diverse autism genes converge to disrupt shared biological pathways, study finds
articles.summary: A massive new map of protein interactions in the brain reveals how hundreds of diverse autism mutations disrupt the same biological networks. The findings provide a vital step toward developing targeted therapies for neurodevelopmental conditions.

articles.title: Scientists strip down the LSD molecule to find the exact parts that trigger hallucinations
articles.summary: By systematically stripping down the complex structure of the LSD molecule, scientists have pinpointed the exact components that trigger hallucinations. This breakthrough paves the way for safer, non-hallucinogenic psychiatric treatments that harness the drug’s therapeutic benefits.
